newsitem.title: USA: U S West sues New Mexico regulators.
newsitem.headline: U S West sues New Mexico regulators.

text.p: U S West Inc. said Friday it has filed a lawsuit against New Mexico regulators, alleging they have created artificial subsidies for local telephone service with advertising revenues from its Yellow Pages directories.

U S West contends the practice, known as "imputation," violates the First and Fifth Amendments to the U.S. Constitution. Directory advertising amounts to more than $12.6 million a year, the company said.

The lawsuit was filed in U.S. District Court in New Mexico by U S West Inc. and its subsidiaries, U S West Communications and U S West Marketing Resources Group against the New Mexico Corporation Commission.

"We filed the suit to stop the New Mexico commission from using the outdated concept of offsetting the costs of providing basic U S West Communications phone service with revenues earned by a completely different company, (Marketing Resources Group)," U S West Executive Vice President Jim Stever said in a statement.
"New Mexico law perpetutates this outdated, illogical and unconstitutional hidden subsidy," he added.

Yellow Pages publishing is not part of the telephone services provided by U S West Communications. The company said that most state commissions across the country impute revenues from directory advertising sales to help keep local rates low.

Even though U S West Communications and U S West Marketing Resources Group are separate entities, state law assigns about 30 percent of the revenues earned by Marketing Resources Group from publishing Yellow Pages in the company's service area to U S West Communications for rate-making purposes, the company said.
U S West's stock rose 75 cents to $31.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
